pulls.title: 8389677: RISC-V: Prefer vmv.v.i to zero vector registers
pulls.author: zangcq
pulls.body_excerpt: The RISC-V Optimization Guide recommends using `vmv.v.i vd, 0` to zero a vector register instead of other idioms such as `vxor.vv vd, vd, vd` or `vmv.v.x vd, x0`. Compared with these alternatives, `vmv.v.i` is a pure immediate splat. It does not read a source vector register and does not consume a scalar register read port. As a result, it avoids the false self-dependency introduced by `vxor.vv vd, vd, vd` and the scalar register dependency of `vmv.v.x vd, x0`. pulls.title: 8370131: C2: Improve ReachabilityFence test coverage
pulls.author: 0zzy0sbourne
pulls.body_excerpt: Add a debug-only verification pass for ReachabilityFence (RF) nodes that runs before RF expansion. The pass iterates over all RF nodes in the compiler's list and checks that each node is well-formed: - Has a valid CFG control input - Has a non-null referent of oop type (`oopptr`, `narrowoop`, or `NULL_PTR`) - Is still live in the graph (has at least one use) The verification is invoked in `Compile::Optimize()` right before the RF expansion phase (Phase 2) and is guarded by `#ifdef ASSERT`, so it only runs in debug/fastdebug builds. pulls.title: 8381560: AArch64: Optimize String.equals intrinsic
pulls.author: behrangi
pulls.body_excerpt: This change improves the AArch64 implementation of String.equals by introducing SIMD-based fast paths using SVE and NEON. SVE implementation: - Uses predicated loads and comparisons for short lengths (len < VL) - Uses a full predicated loop for longer inputs - Handles the tail via an overlapped compare at (base + len - VL) NEON implementation: - Uses an 8-byte pre-read to simplify tail handling and eliminate 4/2/1-byte scalar branches - Processes 16-byte chunks using LDP pair loads - Uses CMP/CCMP to collapse comparisons into a single branch on mismatch These changes reduce branch pressure and

pulls.title: 8383246: Add relaxed implementations of atomics for Windows/AArch64
pulls.author: raneashay
pulls.body_excerpt: This patch implements two key changes. First, prior to this patch, the Windows/AArch64 implementation of `PlatformAdd`, `PlatformXchg`, and `PlatformCmpXchg` structs ignored the `atomic_memory_order` parameter and instead used the strongest barrier semantics for all operations. This is correct but unnecessarily conservative and also inconsistent with the Linux and macOS AArch64 ports, both of which dispatch to different instruction sequences based on the requested ordering.
